The retro city: designs for the world view

Draft, 26 October 2026, step 1 of the author's request: the design of each concept, for validation; no animation yet. A 16-bit overworld inspired by, never copied from the SNES-era maps: original pixel art, one small palette (palette.py), chunky outlines, tiled grass, sinuous dirt roads. Every piece is drawn by Python in world/concepts/drafts/retro-city/ as crisp SVG rects, so it stays sharp on a projector. Each building is drawn as separate layers (roof, front wall, side walls, back wall, floor with its interior), shown closed and then open to prove it.

The map

480 x 270 map pixels (16:9), shown here at 3 screen pixels each (1440 px wide); full screen at 1920 x 1080 is 4 each. The road joins the four buildings in the talk's order, read like a book: Motivation top left, Methods top right, then back down to Results bottom left and on to What's next bottom right, across the rails. The walker (A) stands at the hospital's door. Shown with Hospital 1, Factory 1, Stadium 1, Station.

1. Motivation: the hospital

The sign reads MOTIVATION; red cross, white walls, ambulance and helipad say hospital. Open, the floor shows the ward: beds, a desk with a clinical note on a screen, a doctor and a nurse (the use cases).

2. Methods: the factory

The sign reads METHODS. Open, the floor is the method in order on one conveyor: English pages, the translating machine, French pages, then the press that makes the model (translation, then pre-training).

3. Results: the stadium

The sign reads RESULTS, on the scoreboard over the gate. The canopy is one layer and lifts; the near stands and the facade are the wall that drops; the floor is the track with the three runners (CamemBERT, DrBERT, TransBERT-bio-fr in their kits), the finish line and the podium.

4. What is possible / released: three places of departure

The release is the model and corpus given to the world, and what may follow: other languages, other fields. Each option is a place things leave from.

Wording of the sign.
wordingfor
WHAT'S NEXT (drawn)all three; says "possible" and "after this talk" at once, and fits the board in 11 characters.
POSSIBLEmatches the island's name, 8 characters, but reads oddly alone on a building.
DEPARTURESthe station only: the board under it then lists the languages and fields.
SET SAIL / LIFT-OFFthe harbour / the launch pad.

Recommendation: Next 1, the Station, signed WHAT'S NEXT. It is the author's idea and it carries the content without words: the departures board lists languages and fields, each wagon carries one, and the train is visibly leaving the map, so the release reads as a departure. It also continues the road: the walker crosses the rails to reach it, and the train can move in the entry animation. The harbour needs a large patch of water; the launch pad says "launch" but not "other languages and fields".

The walker

Three options, each with four walk frames facing right and a standing pose facing us. Left and up/down walks come from mirroring and from the standing pose.

Layers in every building SVG carry data-layer: ground, shadow, outback, floor, back, left, interior, right, front, roof, outside, smoke. Sources: palette.py (the palette), pix.py (pixels to SVG, the 5x7 and 3x5 fonts), box.py (the layered building), hospital.py, factory.py, stadium.py, fourth.py, avatar.py, props.py, terrain.py, mapview.py, sheet.py.
